problem: RL platforms for embodied navigation run many copies of off-the-shelf single-environment simulators (e.g. Habitat-Sim) on many CPUs/GPUs. This wastes memory (each instance holds gigabytes of scene assets), adds sync/communication overhead, and forces scale-out (e.g. 64 GPUs for 3 days) to reach billions of samples.
motivation: Deep RL for visual navigation needs billions of samples from realistic 3D scans, which is out of reach for most researchers. The simulator is the bottleneck and is treated as a black box, so the paper co-designs the renderer, simulator, policy DNN and optimizer for high-throughput, large-batch execution.
key_idea: Design the simulator and 3D renderer around 'batch simulation': process large batches of environment requests at once, sharing scene assets across environments and amortizing rendering, I/O and synchronization, and pair this with an efficient policy DNN and large-mini-batch optimization.
insight: Most of the speedup comes from batch simulation itself, not the small network. BPS-R50 is still over 10x faster than the DD-PPO baseline with the same ResNet50 encoder and 128px input (2,300 vs 180 FPS), and BPS is 4.5-7.8x faster than the Habitat-Sim baseline given the same small DNN (depth agents). Asset sharing allows much larger N, which raises GPU utilization across all components (RGB is slower than depth mainly because its smaller N is forced by texture memory). Large-batch tricks (sqrt LR scaling, Lamb) recover sample efficiency; Lamb is +1.5% SPL ahead of Adam at 1B samples.
method: Batch simulator: CPU navmesh/geodesic computations for N environments (N >> cores), scheduled dynamically on a thread pool, results written to per-environment slots and passed as one batched request.
Batch renderer: combines the draw commands of all N environments into a single Vulkan rendering request, with each environment's view a tile of one big frame, avoiding pipeline flushes.
Scene asset sharing: K << N unique scenes in GPU memory (N/K <= 32), shared across environments and rotated by asynchronous loading that overlaps rollouts and learning.
Pipelined geometry culling: GPU compute-shader frustum culling pipelined with rasterization of other environments to raise GPU utilization when most triangles are sub-pixel.
Efficient policy DNN: 64x64 input, 9-layer SE-ResNet with a SpaceToDepth stem, no normalization layers (Fixup init), LSTM, half-precision inference and mixed-precision training.
Large mini-batch PPO: LR scaled by sqrt(B/256) with no warmup, and Lamb optimizer with an extra trust-ratio clip rho; one PPO epoch with 2 mini-batches; DD-PPO for multi-GPU with per-GPU N=128.

setting.backbone: SE-ResNet9 + LSTM policy (trained from scratch with PPO/DD-PPO); variant BPS-R50 uses ResNet50
setting.training_data: 2.5B simulated frames of PointGoal RL in Gibson-2plus (depth) and Gibson + Matterport3D (RGB); Flee/Explore on AI2-THOR in an appendix
setting.observation: 64x64 depth or RGB (128x128 in some variants, rendered at 256 and downsampled) + GPS/compass
setting.action_space: low-level: forward 0.25 m, turn left/right 10°, stop
setting.simulator: custom batch simulator/renderer (BPS); evaluation in Habitat-Sim

numbers_note: Throughput results (FPS, e.g. 19,900 on a single RTX 3090 for depth, 72,000 on 8x2080Ti) are in Table 1 and are not captured in the SR/SPL schema.
results: BPS trains depth agents at 19,900 FPS on one RTX 3090 (110x faster than the DD-PPO/Habitat-Sim baseline at 180 FPS), and up to 72,000 FPS on 8 GPUs. It reaches SPL 94.4 (val) / 91.5 (test) for depth versus 95.6 / 94.4 for the baseline, and 88.4 / 83.7 for RGB versus 92.9 / 92.0, i.e. about 97% of baseline accuracy for depth and 91% for RGB. On a single RTX 3090, BPS reaches over 80% SPL in 10 h, while the baseline reaches only 40%.
limitations: Slightly lower final accuracy than the ResNet50 baseline, especially for RGB (test SPL 83.7 vs 92.0).
Large aggregate batches hurt sample efficiency, so per-GPU batch size must shrink in multi-GPU runs, giving imperfect scaling (up to 5.6x on 8 GPUs).
RGB textures consume GPU memory and force smaller N; the system covers only PointNav-style navigation and static scenes, with no physics.
